items.headline: HK banks and tech slide on first trading day back from Golden Week: HSBC -5%, StanChart -5.5%, Hang Seng Tech hits 2-year low
items.summary: The Hang Seng Index fell 1.43% to 23,785.79, breaching 24,000, as HSBC and Standard Chartered tumbled roughly 5% and 5.5% on surging global bond yields, UK budget tax-hike fears (HSBC derives ~22% of profit from the UK vs ~3-5% for StanChart) and an FT report that HSBC plans to cut ~70% of UK wealth-advisor roles for AI. The Hang Seng Tech sub-index closed at 4,073.38, its lowest level since September 2024, even as southbound Stock Connect flows were net positive at HK$6.48B.
items.actionable: This is a bank-led, UK-tax/rate-driven selloff rather than a China-specific event, but it compounds the existing HK tech de-rating, so size HSBC/StanChart-adjacent and Hang Seng Tech exposure for continued volatility into UK budget headlines.

items.headline: Iran's Hormuz tanker attacks intensify; Brent jumps to $103.79, WTI to $91.11, Rubio says Iran 'lost complete control' of the strait
items.summary: UKMTO logged nine tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz during October, including a strike on the 'On Peace' tanker off Oman that set it ablaze; traffic through the strait, which carries ~20% of global seaborne oil, fell to its lowest level in over two months. Brent crude rose 3.58% to $103.79/bbl and WTI rose 3.21% to $91.11/bbl as a result, with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stating Iran had 'lost complete control' of the waterway, a claim Tehran disputes.
items.actionable: Geopolitically-driven oil strength adds inflation pressure that reinforces the Fed's hawkish tilt (a mild headwind for gold/silver and risk assets broadly via higher-for-longer yields), while also being the proximate trigger for Thursday's equity/crypto risk-off -- no direct SGX read-through beyond general sentiment.

items.headline: US stocks fall as crude spikes and chip stocks weigh; CNN Fear & Greed drops to 38 (Fear) from 47 (Neutral)
items.summary: The S&P 500 closed down 0.47% at 7,765.36 and the Nasdaq fell 1.25% to 27,193.34 on Thursday as the Hormuz-driven crude spike and semiconductor weakness offset earlier-week record highs; VIX ticked up 2.19% to 15.41, still a low-vol reading. CNN's Fear & Greed Index fell sharply to 38 (Fear) as of the Thursday close from Wednesday's 47 (Neutral), with 52-week new lows now outnumbering new highs roughly 4-to-1 on the NYSE.
items.actionable: The sentiment swing to outright Fear alongside deteriorating breadth (new lows swamping new highs) is a near-term risk-off signal worth noting for timing adds to the silver/gold-miner and HK tech books, even though the VIX itself remains in low-vol territory.

items.headline: Singapore STI falls 1.22% as DBS, OCBC, UOB slide in sympathy with the global bank selloff
items.summary: The Straits Times Index fell at Thursday's open as banking counters led declines. On VERIFIED 8 Oct closes from this book's own price spine: DBS closed S$73.85, down 4.70% from 77.49, and OCBC closed S$29.00, down 4.29% from 30.30. UOB (U11.SI) is not carried in the spine, so no level is quoted for it. The move tracked the HSBC/Standard Chartered-led global bank selloff on surging bond yields. REITs were comparatively resilient, with CapitaLand Ascendas REIT up slightly.
items.actionable: The SGX bank book (DBS/OCBC/UOB) is now trading on the same global yields/NIM narrative hitting HSBC and StanChart, compounding the prior OCBC-specific Citi downgrade -- treat this as a sector-wide rate-sensitivity story rather than an SGX-specific issue, with REITs/developers comparatively insulated so far.
items.priceNote: corrected 2026-10-09: the original summary quoted intraday 'at the open' levels — DBS 'fell 2.32% to S$75.69' and OCBC 'slipped to S$29.77' — which understated the DBS move by half against the verified 8 Oct close of 73.85 (-4.70%). The price gate blocked publish on the OCBC figure; the DBS figure was wrong too and the gate did not catch it, because an intraday level can sit inside the day's high/low while still misdescribing what happened. Levels are now verified closes only.

items.headline: Bitcoin extends slide to ~$81,845 as risk-off from yields, oil and the Fed minutes continues
items.summary: Bitcoin fell a further 1.72% to roughly $81,845, continuing the slide from above $86,000 earlier in the week, as rising Treasury yields, the Hormuz-driven oil spike and hawkish Fed minutes kept broad risk assets under pressure. The crypto Fear & Greed Index eased to 64 (Greed) from 71 as the market digests the pullback, though it has not flipped to Fear.
items.actionable: Crypto continues trading as a high-beta risk-off proxy alongside gold/silver miners and equities rather than a safe haven; the multi-day grind lower alongside Thursday's broader Fear & Greed drop to 38 suggests continued correlated downside risk rather than a crypto-specific shock.

items.headline: Fed minutes confirm hawkish September hike to 3.75%-4.00%, dot plot flags one more hike in 2026
items.summary: Minutes released Oct 7 from the Fed's Sept 15-16 meeting confirmed Chair Kevin Warsh led a unanimous 12-0 vote to raise rates 25bp to 3.75%-4.00% (first hike since 2023), citing elevated inflation. The September dot plot showed a majority of officials expecting another hike before year-end, more hawkish than markets had priced.
items.actionable: The hawkish Fed repricing remains the biggest macro risk to the silver/gold miner book and crypto exposure, so size and stop-loss decisions on GDX/SLVP/SILJ/AG should assume continued USD strength and yield pressure rather than an imminent pivot, especially now that it is compounding with Hormuz-driven oil/inflation risk.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export-control truce nears Nov 10 expiry; Congress races a 4-bill package before the deadline
items.summary: The one-year suspension of China's expanded rare-earth export controls lapses Nov 10, 2026, with Beijing giving no public signal on renewal; roughly $6.5T of Western EV, chip and defense output is estimated exposed if fuller controls snap back. Congress has assembled a four-bill package (domestic mining acceleration, a federally-backed mineral stockpile, and defense-program protections) aiming to pass before the deadline, while yttrium oxide prices outside China have already risen ~140x since April 2025 export licensing began.
items.actionable: A hard expiry without renewal would be a strong bullish catalyst for the rare-earth watchlist (MP Materials, Lynas, Energy Fuels) as Western buyers scramble for non-China supply -- worth setting a calendar alert for Nov 10 and tracking the Congressional package's progress as a secondary catalyst.

items.headline: MP Materials to deliver GM's first non-China rare-earth magnets; Lynas inks ~$96m Pentagon offtake
items.summary: MP Materials is about to deliver General Motors' first rare-earth magnets made outside China, from its Texas facility, backed by the Pentagon's $400m preferred-equity stake, a $150m loan, and a 10-year commitment to buy NdPr output at a $110/kg floor. Separately, Lynas Rare Earths agreed to sell roughly $96m of light and heavy rare earths to the US Department of War over four years, referencing the same $110/kg NdPr floor.
items.actionable: Both watchlist names now have government-backed, price-floored revenue streams independent of spot rare-earth pricing, which de-risks the long thesis on MP/Lynas even if China eases export controls.

items.headline: OCBC sheds 5.8% (~S$8b market cap) after Citi downgrade to Sell
items.summary: Citi cut OCBC from Neutral to Sell with a price target well below its pre-downgrade trading level, flagging flat Q3 YoY earnings, a 35-70bp net interest margin hit from repricing SGD fixed deposits, and 'misplaced optimism' on Singapore rates after OCBC's P/E expanded 46% this year. OCBC was the most heavily traded SGX stock that day at over S$459m turnover.
items.actionable: This is an analyst downgrade on NIM-compression and valuation grounds, now compounded by Thursday's broader global-bank selloff hitting DBS/OCBC/UOB together -- reassess the position on earnings/margin fundamentals and the global rates backdrop rather than treating either move in isolation as a red flag requiring an exit.

items.headline: Energy Fuels tumbles 9% as uranium/advanced-reactor names sell off together
items.summary: Energy Fuels (UUUU) fell 9% to $10.27, with Oklo and Centrus Energy down 5% each and the Global X Uranium ETF (URA) off 5%, even as the S&P 500 was roughly flat, indicating sector-specific selling tied to concerns that nuclear-buildout valuations are pricing in revenue that is still years away.
items.actionable: This is a uranium/nuclear-theme de-rating (Oklo, Centrus fell in tandem), not company-specific bad news, so it does not change the rare-earth/uranium diversification thesis but confirms high beta to nuclear-sector sentiment swings.

items.headline: Gold ($4,164) and silver ($59.64) hold up near recent levels despite Fed hawkishness and risk-off
items.summary: Gold edged up 0.57% to $4,164.30/oz and silver was roughly flat at $59.64/oz (-0.43%), both well off January 2026's ~$121/oz silver record and October's highs, but stabilizing even as the hawkish Fed minutes and a stronger dollar pressured the complex earlier in the week. Global gold ETFs posted a record $31B in Q3 2026 inflows per the World Gold Council, led by US and UK funds.
items.actionable: The stabilization alongside record quarterly ETF inflows suggests the physical/structural bid under gold persists despite the yields/dollar headwind -- treat current levels as a macro-driven consolidation rather than a break in the silver squeeze/deficit thesis underpinning the miner book.

items.headline: No active US government shutdown -- stopgap funding runs to Dec 11, 2026
items.summary: A continuing resolution signed into law Sept 2, 2026 funds federal agencies through Dec 11, 2026, averting the widely-watched October shutdown risk; Congress is in recess until a Nov 9 lame-duck session where funding, LIHEAP and the farm bill must be resolved. Status reconfirmed as of this run.
items.actionable: No shutdown is active right now, though the Dec 11 funding cliff and the Nov 9 lame-duck session are both worth re-flagging as they approach, particularly alongside the overlapping Nov 10 rare-earth truce deadline.
